description: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) between two models—NESAC ft model (orange) and SESHA ft model (green)—when applied to various optimisations, with the results compared against the Whisper large model. The horizontal axis represents the "Difference in Average WER from Whisper large," with values ranging from 0.000 to 0.004, while the vertical axis lists the optimisations applied: "Dates," "Americanisms," "Remove Spacing," "Add Spacing," and "Normalised." For each optimisation, two bars are shown: the orange bar for the NESAC ft model and the green bar for the SESHA ft model. The chart shows that the SESHA ft model consistently has a lower WER than the NESAC ft model across all five optimisations. The largest difference in WER is observed for the "Normalised" optimisation, where the NESAC ft model has a difference of 0.00334 and the SESHA ft model has a difference of 0.00323. The smallest difference is for the "Dates" optimisation, with the NESAC ft model at 0.00257 and the SESHA ft model at 0.00228. The WER differences for the "Americanisms" optimisation are 0.00299 for the NESAC ft model and 0.00302 for the SESHA ft model. For "Remove Spacing," the differences are 0.00311 and 0.00306, respectively. For "Add Spacing," the differences are 0.00319 and 0.00344. The bars are sorted in descending order of the WER difference for the NESAC ft model.
